newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle owners and packer buyers were at a standoff on Monday, with no reported sales, feedlot sources said.
Bids were light and ranged from $67.00 to $69.00 per cwt but were passed by owners pricing cattle from $70.00 to $73.00, they said. The majority of offers were at $71.00, the sources said.

Fed cattle prices last week rallied $3.00 compared with the previous week, with a top of $69.00 in active volume. Brisk sales supplied packers with adequate numbers of cattle inventories for this week, they said.
Sales this week were not expected until Wednesday or Thursday as packers work through the live inventories, the sources said.
Prices were expected to remain unchanged at $69.00, but could turn higher if beef demand continues strong, they said.

Showlists for this week were mostly smaller. Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlot showlists were estimated near 84,000 head, about 1,000 lower than last week, market sources said. Kansas showlists were pegged near 75,000 head, up about 6,000. Nebraska's showlist was estimated near 65,000 head, down about 10,000, they said.
